Give your answer as an integer number of thousands of parcels.

questions.trap: Reading the top of each stacked bar rather than the Warehouse band uses the company totals 280 and 400, giving 400 * 1,100 - 280 * 900 = 188,000, and an answer of 188. In a stacked bar the top edge is the cumulative total, not the value of the top or bottom segment.

questions.explanation: Warehouse grew from 140 to 210, an increase of 70, so the percent increase is 70/140 = 0.5, or 50 percent. Transport grew from 80 to 120, an increase of 40, so the percent increase is 40/80 = 0.5, or 50 percent. Both quantities equal 50 percent, so the two quantities are equal.
questions.trap: Comparing the raw increases, 70 employees against 40 employees, makes Column A look larger and yields choice A. A larger absolute increase does not mean a larger percent increase, because Warehouse starts from a much larger base.

questions.explanation: Aster is at least 50 percent greater than Borel exactly when Aster is at least 1.5 times Borel. January: 1.5 * 240 = 360 and Aster is 120, no. June: 1.5 * 120 = 180 and Aster is 320, yes. So March, May and June qualify.
questions.trap: March is the trap: Aster's 240 is exactly 1.5 times Borel's 160, so Aster is exactly 50 percent greater. Students who require a strict inequality drop March and select only May and June.

questions.trap: Reporting the percent CHANGE in Aster's share gives (63.64 - 44.44)/44.44 = 43 percent, not 19. A difference of two percents is measured in percentage points and is a plain subtraction, with no division by p.

The amount the library allocated to Collections in 2024 was approximately what percent greater than the amount it allocated to Collections in 2023?

questions.explanation: Collections received 30 percent of the 2024 budget: 0.30 * $1,500,000 = $450,000. The table gives the 2023 Collections figure as $380,000. The increase is $450,000 - $380,000 = $70,000, and the percent increase is 70,000/380,000 = 0.1842, which is about 18 percent.
questions.trap: Dividing the $70,000 increase by the 2024 amount gives 70,000/450,000 = 15.6 percent, which rounds to choice A, 16 percent. The base for a percent increase is the earlier amount, $380,000.

The circle graph shows how Fenwick Municipal Library allocated its 2024 operating budget of $1,500,000 among five categories, and the table below it gives the amount, in dollars, that each category received in 2023.

Column A: Facilities' 2024 allocation as a percent of the library's total 2024 budget
Column B: Facilities' 2023 allocation as a percent of the library's total 2023 budget

options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column A is read straight off the circle graph: Facilities took 15 percent of the 2024 budget. For Column B, the chart prints the 2023 total as $1,280,000 (and the five table entries confirm it), and Facilities received $200,000 of that, so its share is 200,000/1,280,000 = 0.15625, or 15.625 percent. Since 15.625 is greater than 15, Column B is greater.
questions.trap: Comparing dollars instead of shares makes Column A look bigger: Facilities got 0.15 * 1,500,000 = $225,000 in 2024 against $200,000 in 2023, which points to choice A. A larger dollar amount out of a much larger budget can still be a smaller share of it.

questions.question:
The circle graph shows how Fenwick Municipal Library allocated its 2024 operating budget of $1,500,000 among five categories, and the table below it gives the amount, in dollars, that each category received in 2023.

Suppose that in 2025 the library increases the Programs allocation by 60 percent over its 2024 amount and leaves every other category at its 2024 amount. Under that plan, Programs would account for what percent of the library's total 2025 budget?

Give your answer to the nearest whole number of percent.

Total 2024 budget: $1,500,000</text><text x="230" y="300">2023 allocation, in dollars</text><text x="230" y="424">Total 2023 budget: $1,280,000</text></g><text x="328.9" y="139.9" text-anchor="start">Staffing 40%</text><text x="277.2" y="264.7" text-anchor="start">Technology 5%</text><text x="168.9" y="256.1" text-anchor="end">Collections 30%</text><text x="131.1" y="139.9" text-anchor="end">Programs 10%</text><text x="182.8" y="79.3" text-anchor="end">Facilities 15%</text><text x="130" y="326">Staffing</text><text text-anchor="end" x="330" y="326">520,000</text><text x="130" y="344">Collections</text><text text-anchor="end" x="330" y="344">380,000</text><text x="130" y="362">Facilities</text><text text-anchor="end" x="330" y="362">200,000</text><text x="130" y="380">Programs</text><text text-anchor="end" x="330" y="380">120,000</text><text x="130" y="398">Technology</text><text text-anchor="end" x="330" y="398">60,000</text></g><path d="M120 308H340M120 406H340" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/></svg>
questions.explanation: Programs received 10 percent of $1,500,000 in 2024, which is $150,000. Raising it by 60 percent gives 1.6 * 150,000 = $240,000. The other four categories keep their 2024 amounts, which total 1,500,000 - 150,000 = $1,350,000, so the 2025 budget is 1,350,000 + 240,000 = $1,590,000. Programs' share is 240,000/1,590,000 = 0.1509, which rounds to 15 percent.
questions.trap: Multiplying the 10 percent share directly by 1.6 gives 16 percent. That treats the total budget as fixed, but the extra $90,000 also enlarges the denominator, so the true share is 15 percent, not 16 percent.

questions.question:
The bar graph shows the average (arithmetic mean) score on a certification exam at each of four testing centres. The value n printed below each bar is the number of candidates who took the exam at that centre. Every one of the 200 candidates took the exam at exactly one of the four centres.

What is the average (arithmetic mean) score of all 200 candidates?
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 480 320" width="480" height="320" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><text x="240" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">Average Certification Exam Score by Testing Centre</text><path d="M62 242H458M62 204H458M62 166H458M62 128H458M62 90H458M62 52H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/><g stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="#e5edf7"><rect x="89" y="67.2" width="58" height="174.8"/><rect x="173" y="82.4" width="58" height="159.6"/><rect x="257" y="97.6" width="58" height="144.4"/><rect x="341" y="120.4" width="58" height="121.6"/></g><path d="M62 52V242 H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><g font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="12" fill="#1f2937"><text x="56" y="246" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="56" y="208" text-anchor="end">20</text><text x="56" y="170" text-anchor="end">40</text><text x="56" y="132" text-anchor="end">60</text><text x="56" y="94" text-anchor="end">80</text><text x="56" y="56" text-anchor="end">100</text><text x="118" y="61.2" text-anchor="middle">92</text><text x="118" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Alder</text><text x="118" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 20</text><text x="202" y="76.4" text-anchor="middle">84</text><text x="202" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Birch</text><text x="202" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 30</text><text x="286" y="91.6" text-anchor="middle">76</text><text x="286" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Cedar</text><text x="286" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 50</text><text x="370" y="114.4" text-anchor="middle">64</text><text x="370" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Dorn</text><text x="370" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 100</text><text x="260" y="300" text-anchor="middle">Testing centre (n = number of candidates)</text><text transform="rotate(-90 16 150)" x="16" y="150" text-anchor="middle">Average score (points)</text></g></svg>
questions.explanation: Because the centres hold different numbers of candidates, the overall mean is a weighted mean. Total points scored: Alder 20 * 92 = 1,840; Birch 30 * 84 = 2,520; Cedar 50 * 76 = 3,800; Dorn 100 * 64 = 6,400. The sum is 14,560 points over 200 candidates, so the mean is 14,560/200 = 72.8.
questions.trap: Averaging the four bar heights gives (92 + 84 + 76 + 64)/4 = 79.0, choice C. That treats the four centres as equally sized, but Dorn alone holds half of all candidates and pulls the true mean well below 79.

questions.question:
The bar graph shows the average (arithmetic mean) score on a certification exam at each of four testing centres. The value n printed below each bar is the number of candidates who took the exam at that centre. Every one of the 200 candidates took the exam at exactly one of the four centres.

Column A: The total number of points scored by all candidates at Dorn
Column B: The total number of points scored by all candidates at Alder, Birch and Cedar combined
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 480 320" width="480" height="320" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><text x="240" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">Average Certification Exam Score by Testing Centre</text><path d="M62 242H458M62 204H458M62 166H458M62 128H458M62 90H458M62 52H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/><g stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="#e5edf7"><rect x="89" y="67.2" width="58" height="174.8"/><rect x="173" y="82.4" width="58" height="159.6"/><rect x="257" y="97.6" width="58" height="144.4"/><rect x="341" y="120.4" width="58" height="121.6"/></g><path d="M62 52V242 H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><g font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="12" fill="#1f2937"><text x="56" y="246" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="56" y="208" text-anchor="end">20</text><text x="56" y="170" text-anchor="end">40</text><text x="56" y="132" text-anchor="end">60</text><text x="56" y="94" text-anchor="end">80</text><text x="56" y="56" text-anchor="end">100</text><text x="118" y="61.2" text-anchor="middle">92</text><text x="118" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Alder</text><text x="118" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 20</text><text x="202" y="76.4" text-anchor="middle">84</text><text x="202" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Birch</text><text x="202" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 30</text><text x="286" y="91.6" text-anchor="middle">76</text><text x="286" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Cedar</text><text x="286" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 50</text><text x="370" y="114.4" text-anchor="middle">64</text><text x="370" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Dorn</text><text x="370" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 100</text><text x="260" y="300" text-anchor="middle">Testing centre (n = number of candidates)</text><text transform="rotate(-90 16 150)" x="16" y="150" text-anchor="middle">Average score (points)</text></g></svg>
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: A centre's total points equal its average score times its number of candidates. Column A: Dorn contributes 100 * 64 = 6,400 points. Column B: Alder 20 * 92 = 1,840, Birch 30 * 84 = 2,520 and Cedar 50 * 76 = 3,800, for a combined 8,160 points. Since 8,160 is greater than 6,400, Column B is greater.
questions.trap: Dorn's 100 candidates exactly match the 20 + 30 + 50 = 100 candidates at the other three centres, so a student who compares only the head counts concludes the totals are equal and picks C. Equal group sizes do not give equal point totals when the averages differ.

questions.question:
The bar graph shows the average (arithmetic mean) score on a certification exam at each of four testing centres. The value n printed below each bar is the number of candidates who took the exam at that centre. Every one of the 200 candidates took the exam at exactly one of the four centres.

Indicate all of the following statements that are true.
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 480 320" width="480" height="320" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><text x="240" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="13" fill="#1f2937">Average Certification Exam Score by Testing Centre</text><path d="M62 242H458M62 204H458M62 166H458M62 128H458M62 90H458M62 52H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/><g stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="#e5edf7"><rect x="89" y="67.2" width="58" height="174.8"/><rect x="173" y="82.4" width="58" height="159.6"/><rect x="257" y="97.6" width="58" height="144.4"/><rect x="341" y="120.4" width="58" height="121.6"/></g><path d="M62 52V242 H458" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><g font-family="Georgia, serif" font-size="12" fill="#1f2937"><text x="56" y="246" text-anchor="end">0</text><text x="56" y="208" text-anchor="end">20</text><text x="56" y="170" text-anchor="end">40</text><text x="56" y="132" text-anchor="end">60</text><text x="56" y="94" text-anchor="end">80</text><text x="56" y="56" text-anchor="end">100</text><text x="118" y="61.2" text-anchor="middle">92</text><text x="118" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Alder</text><text x="118" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 20</text><text x="202" y="76.4" text-anchor="middle">84</text><text x="202" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Birch</text><text x="202" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 30</text><text x="286" y="91.6" text-anchor="middle">76</text><text x="286" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Cedar</text><text x="286" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 50</text><text x="370" y="114.4" text-anchor="middle">64</text><text x="370" y="260" text-anchor="middle">Dorn</text><text x="370" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11">n = 100</text><text x="260" y="300" text-anchor="middle">Testing centre (n = number of candidates)</text><text transform="rotate(-90 16 150)" x="16" y="150" text-anchor="middle">Average score (points)</text></g></svg>
options: A. The average score of all 200 candidates was less than 75.
B. The combined number of candidates at Alder and Birch was greater than the number of candidates at Dorn.
C. The combined average score of the candidates at Alder and Birch exceeded the combined average score of the candidates at Cedar and Dorn by more than 18 points.
D. The number of candidates at Dorn was more than 3 times the number of candidates at Birch.
E. The average score at Birch was 20 percent greater than the average score at Dorn.
F. The average score of all 200 candidates was greater than the median of the four centre averages.
questions.explanation: The weighted totals are Alder 1,840, Birch 2,520, Cedar 3,800 and Dorn 6,400, summing to 14,560 points over 200 candidates. A: the overall mean is 14,560/200 = 72.8, which is less than 75, so A is true. B: Alder and Birch hold 20 + 30 = 50 candidates against Dorn's 100, so B is false. C: Alder and Birch average (1,840 + 2,520)/50 = 87.2 while Cedar and Dorn average (3,800 + 6,400)/150 = 68.0, a gap of 19.2 points, which exceeds 18, so C is true. A student who ignores the candidate counts and averages the bar heights instead gets 88 against 70, a gap of exactly 18, which does not exceed 18 - so this option separates the weighted method from the unweighted one. D: 3 * 30 = 90 and Dorn has 100 candidates, so D is true. E: (84 - 64)/64 = 31.25 percent, not 20 percent, so E is false. F: the median of 92, 84, 76 and 64 is (84 + 76)/2 = 80, and 72.8 is less than 80, so F is false.
questions.trap: Statement E catches students who subtract the bar heights, get 84 - 64 = 20, and read that gap of 20 points as '20 percent greater'. A percent comparison divides by the base, and 20/64 = 31.25 percent, so E must be left unselected.
